:::{#thm-cond-lotus}
#### Conditional LOTUS, discrete case

Let $X$ and $Y$ be jointly distributed discrete random variables,
$h$ a function of two arguments,
$W \eqdef h(X, Y)$,
and $x$ a value with $\P(X = x) > 0$.
Then $W$ is discrete,
and $\E{h(X, Y) \mid X = x}$ from @def-cond-expectation-general
equals $\E{W \mid X = x}$ from @def-cond-expectation,
with one sum converging absolutely exactly when the other does.

:::

::: proof

$W$ is discrete because its range is contained in
$\set{h(u, y) : u \in \rangef{X},\, y \in \rangef{Y}}$,
which is countable.
For each $w \in \rangef{W}$,
the event $\set{X = x,\, W = w}$ is the disjoint union
of the events $\set{X = x,\, Y = y}$ over the values $y \in \rangef{Y}$ with $h(x, y) = w$, so:

$$
\ba
\P(W = w \mid X = x)
&= \frac{\P(X = x,\, W = w)}{\P(X = x)}
&& \text{(conditional PMF of } W \text{)} \\
&= \frac{1}{\P(X = x)} \sum_{\substack{y \in \rangef{Y} \\ h(x, y) = w}} \P(X = x,\, Y = y)
&& \text{(countable additivity over the disjoint events } \set{X = x,\, Y = y} \text{)} \\
&= \sum_{\substack{y \in \rangef{Y} \\ h(x, y) = w}} \P(Y = y \mid X = x)
&& \text{(divide each term; conditional PMF of } Y \text{)}
\ea
$$

Every $y \in \rangef{Y}$ with $\P(Y = y \mid X = x) > 0$
has $h(x, y) \in \rangef{W}$,
because some outcome has $X = x$ and $Y = y$, and $W = h(x, y)$ there;
the other values of $y$ contribute terms equal to $0$.
So the groups $\set{y \in \rangef{Y} : h(x, y) = w}$, over $w \in \rangef{W}$,
contain every $y$ with a non-zero term, each exactly once:

$$
\ba
\E{W \mid X = x}
&= \sum_{w \in \rangef{W}} w \cd \P(W = w \mid X = x)
&& \text{(conditional expectation of } W \text{)} \\
&= \sum_{w \in \rangef{W}} w \cd \sum_{\substack{y \in \rangef{Y} \\ h(x, y) = w}} \P(Y = y \mid X = x)
&& \text{(the display above)} \\
&= \sum_{w \in \rangef{W}} \sum_{\substack{y \in \rangef{Y} \\ h(x, y) = w}} w \cd \P(Y = y \mid X = x)
&& \text{(distribute } w \text{ into the inner sum)} \\
&= \sum_{w \in \rangef{W}} \sum_{\substack{y \in \rangef{Y} \\ h(x, y) = w}} h(x, y) \cd \P(Y = y \mid X = x)
&& \text{(} w = h(x, y) \text{ for every term of the inner sum)} \\
&= \sum_{y \in \rangef{Y}} h(x, y) \cd \P(Y = y \mid X = x)
&& \text{(the groups contain every non-zero term once)} \\
&= \E{h(X, Y) \mid X = x}
&& \text{(conditional expectation of a function of } X \text{ and } Y \text{)}
\ea
$$

The same steps with $\abs{w}$ and $\abs{h(x, y)}$ in place of $w$ and $h(x, y)$
regroup a sum of non-negative terms, which is valid whether or not it converges,
so one sum converges absolutely exactly when the other does,
and then the regrouping above is valid too.

:::
